examples.text: Woher weißt du das? Hast du uns etwa belauscht?

glosses: To hear (intentionally) a conversation one is not intended to hear; to listen in.

examples.text: I hope nobody was eavesdropping on our conversation last night, since it got so personal.

glosses: To listen for another organism's calls, so as to exploit them.

examples.text: […] Eastern Red Bat will eavesdrop on the sonar calls of other red bats to locate potential insect prey.
Frog-biting midges also depend on eavesdropping for reproduction, and one would predict similarly strong selection to evolve auditory adaptations for hearing and localizing calls of their hosts.

glosses: The dripping of rain from the eaves of a house.
The space around a house on which such water drips.
A concealed aperture through which an occupant of a building can surreptitiously listen to people talking at an entrance to the building.
The act of intentionally hearing a conversation not intended to be heard.

examples.text: Were you having a little eavesdrop on us last night?

glosses: guhdarî kirin, bi dizî guh dan
